title: A Bengaluru wealth app rebuilt its finfluencer engine on 'process not promises' after SEBI froze it — and beat its pre-crisis CAC
content: SITUATION: A Bengaluru mutual-funds-plus-stocks app (~4.2L MAU) ran 90% of growth through 45 Instagram and YouTube finfluencers. The best-performing hooks were the illegal ones: '12% guaranteed', 'this fund will double your money', screenshots of personal P&L. When SEBI tightened finfluencer norms, compliance flagged 38 of 45 creators as non-compliant and legal froze the entire engine overnight. Installs collapsed from 3,100/day to 1,150/day in three weeks; blended CAC jumped ₹240 to ₹690. ACTION: We rebuilt the creator brief around process, not promises. Hooks shifted to 'how SIP rupee-cost-averaging works', 'why I rebalance every March', 'ELSS vs PPF for 80C'. Every video carried the SEBI disclaimer card. We concentrated 60% of spend on 12 vetted creators, added a WhatsApp drip teaching one concept a day, and ran Google Search on intent ('best ELSS 2026') instead of greed. OUTCOME: Over 11 weeks installs reached 7,150/day — 2.3x the pre-crisis baseline of 3,100 — CAC settled at ₹310 — still ₹70 above the pre-freeze ₹240 but less than half the ₹690 crisis peak — and Day-30 SIP activation rose 9% to 17% because educated users converted and stayed.
lesson: In SEBI/RBI/IRDAI-regulated categories, compliance is a positioning filter, not just a legal cost. Returns-promise hooks pull in greed-led tyre-kickers who churn; process-education hooks ('how SIP averaging works') pull higher-intent users who activate and retain. Track Day-30 activation by hook type, not install volume — the 'safe' creative nearly doubled activation (9% to 17%) and beat the banned creative on real cost-per-activated-user. Concentrate spend on a few genuinely compliant creators before regulators force your hand, not after.
